title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 3rd Proof The Uniqueness Of Conveying The Message Summoning And Faith

questions.question: What three strong qualities did the passage say he showed while calling people to the truth?
questions.answer: He showed strong patience, firmness, and bravery.

questions.question: Who stood against him when he was delivering the message?
questions.answer: Powerful governments, other religions, his own people, his tribe, and even his uncle stood against him.

questions.question: How did he act even when so many people opposed him?
questions.answer: He did not pull back or show fear or worry.

questions.question: What result is given as proof of his success in delivering the message?
questions.answer: He challenged the world and Islam became dominant in the world.

questions.question: What does that success show about him?
questions.answer: It shows that no one was like him in bringing the message and inviting people to the truth.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the strength of his faith?
questions.answer: It says his faith was amazingly strong, wide, and full of certainty.

questions.question: What kinds of ideas could not shake his belief?
questions.answer: The beliefs, philosophies, and teachings that were common in the world at that time could not weaken his faith.

questions.question: What feelings were unable to enter his faith?
questions.answer: Doubt, hesitation, weakness, and anxiety could not enter it.

questions.question: Which group is named first among the holy people of later times who benefited from his faith?
questions.answer: The Companions are named first.

questions.question: What did later righteous people think about his level of belief?
questions.answer: They saw him as having the highest level of faith.

questions.question: Why does the traveler decide that lying and cheating do not fit such a person?
questions.answer: Because someone with such a unique religion, worship, prayer, call to truth, and faith would not be a liar or deceiver.

questions.question: What is the main point of this passage?
questions.answer: The main point is that his courage, success, and unmatched faith prove his truthfulness.

questions.question: In this passage, what part of his mission is discussed first?
questions.answer: First, it talks about how he delivered the message and called people to the truth.

questions.question: How serious was the opposition against him?
questions.answer: It was very serious and harsh, coming from many sides.

questions.question: What does the passage show by saying even his relatives opposed him?
questions.answer: It shows that the pressure on him was personal as well as public.

questions.question: Did that pressure make him uncertain in his mission?
questions.answer: No, it did not make him uncertain at all.

questions.question: How is his faith described besides being strong?
questions.answer: It is also described as broad, amazing, and very elevated.

questions.question: What kinds of people and ideas failed to weaken his certainty?
questions.answer: Famous thinkers, religious teachers, and the common beliefs of the time all failed to weaken it.

questions.question: How did the Companions and later saintly people connect to his faith?
questions.answer: They took from his example and saw him as the highest model of belief.

questions.question: Name two areas listed at the end that support his truthfulness.
questions.answer: Two of them are his worship and his call to the truth.

questions.question: What final judgment did the traveler make with his mind?
questions.answer: He became sure that falsehood and trickery could not belong to such a person.

questions.question: What did he keep doing even when many enemies opposed him?
questions.answer: He kept delivering the message and inviting people to the truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about his level of fear during this struggle?
questions.answer: It says he showed no sign of fear.

questions.question: Why is his courage especially impressive in this passage?
questions.answer: Because the opposition came from large powers and also from people close to him.

questions.question: What big achievement is used as evidence for his success?
questions.answer: The spread and dominance of Islam are used as evidence.

questions.question: According to the passage, what conclusion comes from that achievement?
questions.answer: The conclusion is that he had no equal in carrying the message.

questions.question: What word best describes his certainty in faith: shaky, ordinary, or extraordinary?
questions.answer: Extraordinary.

questions.question: What could not place even a small doubt into his heart?
questions.answer: The strong ideas, beliefs, philosophies, and religious teachings around him could not do that.

questions.question: Who are described as the leaders in levels of belief?
questions.answer: The Companions are described that way.

questions.question: How did saintly people after them view him?
questions.answer: They viewed him as the highest example of faith and drew from his belief.

questions.question: What list near the end gathers the reasons for trusting him?
questions.answer: It mentions his sacred law, Islam, worship, prayer, call to truth, and faith.

questions.question: Put the passage’s message in one sentence.
questions.answer: His unmatched courage and unshakable faith show that he was completely truthful.

questions.question: When he invited people to the truth, what personal qualities came out clearly?
questions.answer: His steadiness, strength, and courage came out clearly.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the kind of enemies he faced?
questions.answer: He faced both outside enemies and people from his own community and family.

questions.question: What happened in the end that points to the power of his message?
questions.answer: Islam rose to a place of great strength in the world.

questions.question: How does the passage describe his faith in relation to the whole world?
questions.answer: It says his faith spread light to the whole world.

questions.question: What were some sources of opposition to his belief?
questions.answer: Common worldviews, philosophers, and religious authorities were sources of opposition.

questions.question: Were they able to weaken his trust and assurance?
questions.answer: No, they were not able to weaken them at all.

questions.question: Why are the saintly people of later ages mentioned?
questions.answer: They are mentioned to show that people of deep faith recognized his belief as the highest.

questions.question: What special place do the Companions have in this proof?
questions.answer: They are presented as the first and leading people in high levels of belief.

questions.question: What moral conclusion does the traveler reach about deception?
questions.answer: He concludes that deception cannot belong to someone with those qualities.

questions.question: What work was he doing when his firmness and bravery were seen?
questions.answer: They were seen while he was delivering Allah’s message and calling people to the truth.

questions.question: What does it mean that he did not show anxiety in the face of hostility?
questions.answer: It means he stayed calm and sure instead of becoming fearful or confused.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention his own tribe and uncle?
questions.answer: It mentions them to show that even close relationships did not stop him from the truth.

questions.question: What larger proof is given from the outcome of his mission?
questions.answer: The larger proof is that he overcame opposition and Islam became victorious in the world.

questions.question: How many tiny doubts were others able to place in his faith?
questions.answer: They were not able to place even the smallest doubt in it.

questions.question: What made his faith stand out from others around him?
questions.answer: It had unmatched strength, certainty, trust, and confidence.

questions.question: Who kept benefiting from his faith after his lifetime?
questions.answer: The Companions and holy people of later generations kept benefiting from it.

questions.question: What does the traveler affirm with his intellect at the end?
questions.answer: He affirms that such a person cannot be a liar or a deceiver.

questions.question: Which six areas are gathered together to support that conclusion?
questions.answer: They are his sacred law, Islam, worship, supplication, call to truth, and faith.

questions.question: What two main subjects does this passage focus on?
questions.answer: It focuses on his courage in sharing the message and his unmatched faith.

questions.question: How broad was the opposition against him?
questions.answer: It was very broad, including nations, religions, and even people close to him.

questions.question: What can we understand from his lack of fear and hesitation?
questions.answer: We can understand that he was deeply sincere and certain.

questions.question: What world-level change is mentioned as evidence of his successful mission?
questions.answer: The passage says Islam became the leading power in the world.

questions.question: How is his faith different from normal human confidence?
questions.answer: It is described as extraordinary, deeply certain, and amazingly wide.

questions.question: What failed to shake his confidence?
questions.answer: The dominant beliefs of the time, philosophical ideas, and religious teachings failed to shake it.

questions.question: Why are the Companions important in this passage?
questions.answer: They are important because they are presented as the first and highest examples among believers after him.

questions.question: How did later saintly believers respond to his example?
questions.answer: They followed his path in faith and accepted him as the highest model.

questions.question: What conclusion does the traveler reach from all these signs together?
questions.answer: He concludes that dishonesty has no place in such a person.

questions.question: Which part of his life is not used alone, but joined with others to prove truthfulness?
questions.answer: His worship is joined with his law, prayer, call, and faith to prove truthfulness.

questions.question: What is the central message for readers?
questions.answer: The central message is that his character, courage, and faith are strong proofs that he spoke the truth.
